messages:
julia: FYI — enterprise customer reported sudden 429s this morning during a scheduled nightly job. They say their monthly quota "depleted" at 02:03 CET (local). They're on a paid hosted plan and expect reset at midnight local. Can SRE/billing confirm how monthly anchors are defined?

sam: billing anchor is stored as an UTC date-time on the account. resets happen at 00:00 UTC on the anchor day. not local midnight. can you share account id + anchor date?

julia: acct=67219, anchor date appears 2024-12-03 in the Console. Customer timezone CET -> their local midnight is 23:00 UTC (previous day) or 01:00 UTC depending on DST; they insist it went to 429 at 02:03 CET which would be 01:03 UTC. they had a spike 01:55-02:05 UTC that consumed a lot of tokens.

alex: got a curl snippet from their ops team, reproducer below. they were doing bulk generate with high max_tokens per call.

```
# minimal repro shown to support
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize ..."}], "max_tokens":2048}'
```

Sample error body returned during spike:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "error": {
    "code": "quota_exhausted",
    "message": "Monthly token quota exhausted for billing cycle anchored at 2024-12-03T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

maria: confirmed anchor = 2024-12-03T00:00:00Z (UTC). the behavior matches anchored UTC reset. we don't align resets to customer local time zones. also: no rollover of unused quota, and monthly counters are authoritative source for enforcement.

julia: customer asked whether there's any short-term "burst bucket" for hosted plans — they triggered a single 10-minute spike that ate ~72% of their monthly allowance. Is there any tolerance?

sre-oncall: short answer: rate limits and a token-bucket at the per-second level allow brief bursts within the per-second window, but the monthly counter is separate and has no automatic hidden buffer. for paid hosted customers we can do manual emergency top-ups or move them to committed capacity (Dedicated). if you need exact enforcement details i can paste the kernel of the limiter.

ops-platform: policy note: we can provision a one-off token credit for operational emergencies. requires an approval flow from billing + account team. provide: account id, timeframe, usage CSV and reason. we then create a credit note and apply tokens for the current cycle.

julia: provided the CSV (they included per-request token counts and timestamps). they requested immediate top-up so their jobs could finish.

maria: pre-approved emergency top-up of 150,000 tokens for acct 67219 — ticket INC-3312 created. billing-bot: issue credit now.

billing-bot: Credit applied: CN-2026-7761; tokens_added=150000; new_cycle_balance=34760; note=emergency top-up for nightly job.

julia: customer retried after credit and all jobs completed. they asked what to change to avoid recurrence. suggested guidance sent: 1) schedule heavy batch runs to avoid cycle boundary; 2) lower max_tokens or paginate prompts to reduce token usage; 3) enable Console usage alerts at 60%/85% thresholds with webhook to ops; 4) implement exponential backoff on 429s and a circuit-breaker for sustained failures; 5) consider Dedicated/reserved if predictable heavy bursts are expected.

alex: added concrete backoff suggestion they can paste: ``retry with exponential backoff: initial 500ms, multiply by 2, jitter up to 1000ms, cap retries to 6``. also suggested adding pre-flight usage check using the Console API to query current cycle remaining tokens before running large jobs.

sre-oncall: extra technical detail for thread: monthly quota is an integer counter updated atomically on approval path; transient per-second rate limiter runs independently. you can get inconsistent-seeming behavior if many concurrent workers all start at once and outrun optimistic client-side checks. recommend a small coordination token/semaphore on client side for large fan-out jobs.

julia: customer appreciated the fix and will move heavy jobs to off-peak and add alerts. asked for doc blurb on billing page to state "resets at 00:00 UTC on billing anchor date" and a short FAQ entry about emergency top-ups and Dedicated migration.

ops-platform: filing a doc request; also recommending a banner for accounts with monthly >100k tokens that shows next reset time in UTC and local timezone conversion. tagging @eng-website.

maria: will follow up with the customer about the applied credit and close INC-3312 once billing confirms invoice adjustments.

julia: closing thread, customer back to green, leaving follow-up tasks in ticket. thanks everyone :white_check_mark:

-- end of thread --
